examples.explanation: An empty list returns an empty list.

problem.explanation: Iterate through the input list, keeping track of elements that have already been seen using a set for fast O(1) lookups. Append an element to the result list only if it's not in the seen set.
hints: A standard `set(items)` will remove duplicates but won't preserve order.
Use a set to keep track of items you have seen so far while iterating through the list and building the result.
problem.statement_markdown: Write a function `deduplicate(items: list) -> list` that takes a list and returns a new list with duplicates removed, while preserving the original order of the first occurrence of each item.
problem.title: Deduplicate preserving order
